title: As a creator, I can turn a text prompt into a video clip and iterate on the result without starting from scratch each time
As a creator, I can animate a still image into motion with the subject and composition preserved
As a creator, I can point at a reference video or image and generate new footage in that style
As a creator, a character or scene stays consistent across multiple generated shots, not just within one clip
As a creator, I can extend a clip or regenerate one segment of it without re-rendering the whole video
As a creator, I can replace or restyle an element inside an existing video while the rest of the frame stays intact
As a creator, I can direct camera moves (pan, zoom, orbit, static) instead of accepting whatever motion the model picks
As a marketer, I can paste a script and get a presenter-led video with a stock or custom avatar, no camera or studio
As a marketer, I can create a custom avatar of a real person through a documented consent and verification flow
As a marketer, I can translate a finished video into other languages with the voice and lip sync carried over
As a creator, generated characters speak my dialogue with lip movement matched to the audio
As a creator, I can add generated sound effects, ambient audio, or music matched to the scene in the same tool
As a marketer, I can render the aspect ratios and resolutions my channels need (16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 1080p or above) without external re-encoding
As a creator, I can draft fast in a cheaper mode and upscale the chosen take to final quality
As a marketer, I can see what a generation will cost in credits or dollars before running it, and track spend afterwards
As a developer, concurrency limits and queue behavior for batch rendering are documented, so I can plan a production pipeline
As a marketer, the vendor's terms state clearly whether I can use generated output commercially and who owns it
As a marketer, generated output carries documented provenance signals (C2PA metadata or a disclosed watermark) I can point to
As a marketer, content rules are documented and a blocked generation fails with a stated reason, not silently
As a developer, I can submit a video generation job through a documented API and retrieve the finished asset
As a developer, my system learns a render finished or failed through a webhook or a documented pollable job status
As an AI-native user, an agent can run the full video loop from docs alone: submit the prompt, watch the job, fetch the asset, and report the cost
